texts:
It is our sad duty to inform you that your uncle, Mr. Vittorio Puntanelli - a director known in the film world as Vittorio Corvessani - has passed away.

As a well-known Italian B-movie horror director, he made a small fortune and built up his estate.

From this estate, he has left you his country house near Pignola. He loved spending time in this house, and it was also the place of his tragic and shocking death.

Until you take possession of your inheritance, Albert Gregovics, the elderly caretaker, whom you may remember from your childhood, will look after the house.

Please travel here as soon as possible to see the unusual home of your uncle, receive the keys to the estate, and learn about the parts of his will that concern you. Once this is done, most of our legal duties regarding the inheritance will be complete.

The manor is waiting for you impatiently, Mr. Puntanelli.

Yours sincerely,

titles:
Extract from the Last Will
of Vittorio Puntanelli
texts:
I, Vittorio Puntanelli, known professionally as Vittorio Corvessani, being of sound mind and acting of my own free will, declare the following.
I leave my manor near Pignola, together with its grounds, furniture, and every key belonging to it, to my nephew, Dante Puntanelli. The house shall be his, with all its doors, locked rooms, cellars, and everything he may find within its walls.

My film collection, notes, occult collection, ritual tools, and all objects connected to the ceremonies of the Brotherhood of the Crimson Threshold shall become the property of the Brotherhood.
They shall also have control over the rest of my fortune.

Finally, I leave them something that no earthly court can record as part of an inheritance:
MY SOUL.

If our agreement was genuine, they will know how to claim it.

If they lied to me, Dante would be wise to burn this document and never speak their name again.


Vittorio Puntanelli -Corvessani-

February 2



I was introduced to a group of wealthy, imaginative people who like to play with dark forces.

At first, I found them entertaining. They talked about spirits and other worlds as if these things were completely normal to them, and as if they really understood them.

Then they proved that they weren't just making things up. Black magic is real. If that's true, then perhaps death isn't as final as I once thought.

Before they left tonight, they gave me some Crimson Witchclaw flower seeds. They told me to plant them in the garden in spring because they'll be needed for summonings.

February 26



Today I was in Silvia's room again. I still can't escape the sadness when I think about what happened, even after all these years.

For years, I couldn't bring myself to go inside. Everything was still exactly as she had left it that summer.

In the end, I had the doorway bricked up. Gregovics thought I did it because I couldn't bear to look at the room anymore.

He was partly right. But the room didn't stay empty.

Something very different is taking shape on the other side of the wall now...

March 28



The laboratory is finished. I'm glad that the first part of my plan has become real. Where Silvia's old bedroom used to be, there are now flasks, copper pots, and books that may help me contact her.

I'd do anything to see her again and hear her voice. Anything...

April 10



I managed to summon the spirit of a Portuguese sailor who died long ago. His name is Baltasar de Alvarenga. He was a pirate in the 1780s, until he drowned during a battle in the Mediterranean Sea. He's a strong and cruel creature, but surprisingly obedient as long as he gets clear orders.

I ordered him to guard my bedroom. He won't let anyone inside.

However, he ignores anyone wearing a protection amulet. I made two protection amulets against him. I always keep one with me, and I keep the other in the house for Albert, in case he needs to clean the chimney or tidy up my room.

May 13



Silvia is back. Or rather... I thought I was bringing Silvia back.

God, I wish I hadn't succeeded!

She isn't the way I remember her. Sometimes I can still see my child in her, but there's a monster watching me through her eyes.

It's as if she stayed too long in a place no human should ever return from.

She has moved into the large wardrobe in the sitting room. Under no circumstances
should it be opened!

As long as she's left alone, she stays quiet. If she's disturbed... she'll attack anyone with hatred! She bit me badly last time too.

June 2



I've lost the bathroom. Several spirits have moved in there, and none of them obey me. I have no power over them.

Don't look into the mirror! Something evil lives inside it. If you stare at it for too long, it will stare back at you.

The bathtub has been taken over by the ghosts of three conjoined French prostitutes from the Middle Ages.

They bathe in otherworldly blood, and all three mouths whisper at the same time.

Don't stay near them for too long. They always take a part of you with them!

July 18



Something has gone terribly wrong. I can feel it on the back of my neck.
Getting involved with those fanatics was a mistake. The ritual got out of control. They're asking me to do strange things I don't want to do. But I've tied myself to them now. I may regret it... in fact, I already do.

That thing... I think I can feel its presence as it moves through the house. Hiding in the shadows.

Something came through. And now I fear for my life.

June 19



Since yesterday, I haven't felt safe in my own house.

Just to be safe, I hid one of the outer gate keys next to the pentagram in the courtyard. In case I ever need to leave the house quickly while something is breathing down my neck.

I left the book with the summoning spell recipe on the bookshelf in the sitting room. The potion also needs my top hat, as an object that connects me to the summoning. Without it, the spell won't begin.

I wore that hat for so many years that it almost became a part of me. On film sets, at premieres, in better times.
Magic likes objects that people are attached to. If I have to give a part of myself to something, I'd rather give this than my soul.

August 26



It's in the cracks...

It's there in the corner of my eye when I walk down the hallway and dare to look back.

It follows me when I'm on the stairs.

It stands outside the door while I lie silently in bed, too afraid to move.

I can hear it whispering horrible things from the other side.

It talks about my death...

titles:
The Gospel of
the Crimson Threshold
About the Brotherhood of the Crimson Threshold
texts:
"The visible world is only one side of the wall."
"Death is not a gate. Death is a lock."

"And we hold the key."

The Brotherhood of the Crimson Threshold is not a religion, because it does not ask for faith. It is not a philosophy, because thoughts alone are not enough. The Brotherhood has only one purpose: to prove that other planes exist beyond the world of the living, and that they can be opened with enough will, sacrifice, and knowledge.

Anyone who joins us must leave their old attachments behind. Outside the Brotherhood, there is no family,

friend, lover, or priest who may be told our secrets. Whatever you see beyond the Threshold, you will carry with you until death.

In return, you may see things that other people can only dream about.

You may hear the dead. You may speak with them. You may command them.

And if you look through the open gate for long enough, sooner or later something on the other side will look back at you.

"I carry my name among the living, but I give my secrets to the Threshold. My blood belongs to this world.
My word belongs to the Brotherhood.
And my soul belongs to whoever comes for me from the other side."

About Spirits

A spirit is not simply the memory of a dead person. Parts of the soul that remain after death may become tied
to a place, a person, an object, or a strong emotion.

With the right ritual, these bonds can be used to call the soul back.
Summoned spirits give off cold, and in this world they appear transparent and blue. Some keep their personality and memories, while others carry only a single emotion: hatred, fear, sorrow, or a desire for revenge.
However, no one should expect the dead to think about time, love, or mercy in the same way they did when they were alive.

A properly made "protection amulet" hides the living presence of its wearer from spirits.

Warning: the amulet protects you from them, but it does not make you invulnerable.
To summon them, you need graveyard soil, black candle wax, a piece of a personal object connected to the dead person, a raven feather, and a handful of salt.

About Grave-Walking Giant Spiders

The records of the Brotherhood call these creatures "Brown Weavers."

They are not simply larger versions of earthly spiders. Their bodies come from a cold, dark plane where solid webs cover the ground and no living creature has ever seen sunlight.

A fully grown creature can be as large as a small horse. The ends of its six legs are covered with hook-like poisonous hairs, allowing it to move across walls, ceilings, and smooth stone.

To summon them, burned black silk, bone dust, and fresh animal blood are required.

The book calls these two-legged, bat-like creatures with partly fox-like heads "Blind Winged Ones." They come from one of the darker regions beyond the Threshold.

Their bodies are heavy and bony, with long claws on two powerful legs. In place of arms, they have huge leathery

wings that allow them to travel great distances in a short time. Their small eyes have poor vision, so they mainly find their way through sounds, smells, and the heartbeat of living creatures.
They often wait in high places, on beams, rooftops, and dark corners of ceilings,
then attack their victims from above.
They are mainly attracted by blood, noise, and fear.

To summon one, burned bat bone, black fox fur, three drops of fresh blood, and a handful of cave soil are required.

Every summoning is a two way process beware! For a summoning linked to a specific individual, place an object associated with that person in the center of the pentagram. Then, you may use the potion or the incantation.






The wise summoner does not ask:
"Am I capable of opening the gate?" but rather,
"Will I be able to close it again?"

About Spirits

A dead soul does not like being ordered around, so it is wiser to make it believe that it is returning by its own choice.

A properly prepared summoning potion sends a scent into the spirit world that a soul without a body can recognize even from beyond the grave.

If the mixture turns black for a few moments while boiling, that is a good sign. If it starts boiling backwards, that is less encouraging.

The potion itself only opens a door. Which spirit steps through it is determined by the personal item used in the summoning. The item must have belonged to the person you wish to summon while they were still alive.

Ingredients:

Cat Tail:




A small amount of fur from the end of the tail is enough. Cats are said to have nine lives and to belong to at least three worlds at the same time, which makes them excellent messengers between different planes of existence. The cat itself usually has a different opinion about this.

Crimson Witchclaw:





An extremely rare woody plant with thorny flowers and crimson, spear-shaped petals. Its stem is covered with poisonous thorns.
Its crimson flowers are used to make paralyzing potions, creature-summoning mixtures, and spells that open gates through blood sacrifice. The thorns on its woody stem can also be used as poison.

Swamp Frog Bile Concentrate:






The liquid binds the plant, animal, and spiritual ingredients together. Half a cup is needed. It is most effective when freshly extracted, but if kept in a properly sealed bottle, it can retain its magical properties for years.
Regarding the smell, most alchemists give the same advice: do not breathe it in before use!

Eye of a Lipizzaner Horse:






The horse's eye is needed so the potion can "see" what the human eye can no longer sense.
No other kind of eye will work. A horse can sense a presence that a human usually notices only when it is already too late.
Preserved in liquid, it keeps for a long time.

Amazonian Swamp Soil:






Where water, earth, decay, and life exist together, the boundaries between worlds are naturally thinner.

Half a handful is enough. Too much soil usually causes the potion to summon mud instead of a spirit.

Bring the rat blood base to a boil and cook the listed ingredients together. Then stir the mixture until its surface becomes completely smooth. The ingredients can be added in any order for this spell. Add them one by one to the boiling base:

- Cat Tail
- Crimson Witchclaw
- Swamp Frog Bile Concentrate
- Eye of a Lipizzaner Horse
- Amazonian Swamp Soil

Let fire consume your flesh,
let shadow swallow your soul,
let death seal away your soul.
You are already dead!

text:
It came as a surprise. The letter was from your Italian uncle's lawyers: you have inherited his manor in southern Italy. You vaguely remember spending a few summers there as a child, before your parents moved across the ocean. Now you have left New York to satisfy your curiosity and deal with the inheritance in person.

As you travelled through the beautiful Italian countryside, the small villages, frozen in time, slowly filled you with a dreamlike calm. Tangled olive groves and rich vineyards cover the sunny hills, ancient castle ruins watch from above, and around here it sometimes feels as if wine really flows like water.

But now you are here.

The old house servant let you in and greeted you as if you had never really left. The afternoon sunlight barely reaches through the heavy curtains. Inside, the house is cool, still, and strangely quiet. The dark manor surrounds you like a giant insect, pressing down on you as if it decided the moment you arrived that it would never let you leave.

“Good to see a familiar face, young master,” says Albert Gregovics. “Dark days have come to this place since your uncle passed away. It is good to have you back after all these years. Feel free to look around. I mean... of course, the manor belongs to you now. I will prepare dinner, but it is getting rather late. Allow me to return to my room. We can talk later.”

With these quietly spoken words, Gregovics disappears down the hallway.

“Your story begins here...”

With great relief, you step through the wrought-iron gate. You have escaped this terrible place!

At first, you keep running until you finally reach the main road. Only then do you dare to stop and look back. You made it out of that cursed place alive.

Dawn is already breaking over the hills, and in the distance you can see the same olive groves, rows of vineyards, and peaceful rooftops you saw when you arrived. But now everything feels different. Now you know the truth. There is something on the other side. You don't know exactly what was released that night. You don't know how many creatures are still inside. And most of all, you don't know if the gate truly closed. But you don't care. You just want to forget all of it!

A church bell rings in the distance...

Feeling a little safer, you turn toward the sound and start walking to the village.

“Your story ends here.”
